# Plan a Weekend Trip From a One-Line Idea With Cohere

> **In short:** A single sentence like "weekend in Portland in October" is enough for Cohere to draft a day-by-day itinerary — but it will invent place names if you let it, so prime it with a short trip-planner instruction first, then tighten the plan one change at a time.

You already know how to send a message in Cohere Chat. This guide teaches a workflow you'll reuse every time you plan a trip: a one-time setup step, a structured first ask, and a series of small follow-ups that tighten the plan into something you can actually use on the day. By the end, you'll have a printable weekend outline and a reusable prompt you can paste into any future trip chat.

## Before you start
- A Cohere account and the chat interface (web or app) you're already using.
- One rough idea of where you want to go and when — even "fall weekend, somewhere coastal" is enough.
- About 15 minutes the first time, around five minutes for future trips once you have the reusable prompt saved.

## Step 1 — Open a new chat and set a trip-planner preamble
Start a fresh conversation so old context doesn't bleed in. Before you type your actual request, look at the top of the chat — there's usually a small field or a collapsible panel for **custom instructions** or a **system message** (sometimes labeled "Persona," or hidden behind a settings icon). Paste a short, plain-English brief: who you are, how detailed you want the answer, and any hard limits. This one-time setup makes every future prompt land better because the model already knows the shape you want.
💬 Example: *"You are a practical trip planner. I travel with one other adult, no kids. We like walking, local food, and one museum or landmark per trip max. Avoid luxury recommendations. Keep each day to three time blocks: morning, afternoon, evening. Never invent specific restaurant names — describe the cuisine and neighborhood instead."*
You'll know it worked when the next reply already feels structured — it begins with a clear "Day 1 / Day 2" layout rather than a wall of suggestions.
If it looks different on your device: if there's no obvious system-prompt field, paste the brief as the very first line of your message instead, prefixed with "Instructions for this chat:" — the effect is similar, just less convenient for reuse.

## Step 2 — Send your one-line trip idea as a structured ask
Now type your vague idea, but wrap it in a request for a specific shape. A bare "weekend in Portland in October" is too open — Cohere will pick a structure for you, and you may not like it. So tell it what shape you want: how many days, what time blocks, what each block should contain. This is the difference between "give me ideas" and "give me a Saturday morning plan with a coffee spot."
💬 Example: *"Weekend trip idea: Portland, Oregon, second weekend of October, two adults, arriving Friday evening, leaving Sunday afternoon. Build a day-by-day plan in three time blocks per day (morning, afternoon, evening). For each block, give: one main activity, one place to eat (describe the cuisine and neighborhood, don't invent names), and a backup if it rains."*
You'll know it worked when the reply comes back split into clearly labeled days and blocks — not a single paragraph of suggestions.
If it looks different on your device: some Cohere views collapse long replies; if you only see the first half, look for a "Show more" or down-arrow at the bottom of the reply.

## Step 3 — Push the answer toward your actual style
The first draft is rarely the one you'd actually use — it's a starting point. Read it once, then ask for one specific change. The most useful follow-ups are about *style*, not content: shorter walks, later mornings, more indoor options, less touristy. Asking for one thing at a time keeps the model from rewriting the whole plan and accidentally undoing the parts you liked.
💬 Example: *"Looks good overall, but tighten this: replace any block that requires a car with a public-transit option, and move any suggestion that starts before 9 a.m. to 10 a.m. or later. Keep everything else the same."*
You'll know it worked when the reply keeps the same structure but only the blocks you asked about actually changed — not the whole plan.
If it looks different on your device: if Cohere offers a thumbs-up/down or a "regenerate" button next to the reply, don't use regenerate here — that gives you a brand-new plan. Instead, send your tweak as a new message in the same chat so the previous version stays visible above it.

## Step 4 — Add a rain backup for one specific slot
Weekend plans live or die by their backup. Pick the *single* most weather-dependent block — usually an outdoor afternoon — and ask for a swap. Naming one slot (not "the whole weekend") keeps the rest of your plan intact and gives you a clean A/B choice for the morning of the trip.
💬 Example: *"For Sunday afternoon only, give me a backup plan that works if it rains: an indoor activity, a nearby warm place for lunch, and a coffee stop I can walk to between them. Keep Saturday exactly as it is."*
You'll know it worked when you see one new afternoon block with three labeled items, and Saturday's plan is unchanged above it.
If it looks different on your device: if Cohere rewrites the whole plan instead of just the one slot, your message probably sounded too general ("give me rain backups") — rephrase to name the day and time block, like "For Sunday afternoon only…"

## Step 5 — Ask for a one-screen summary you can actually use on your phone
Long replies are great for thinking; they're bad for using on the go. Ask Cohere to compress the whole plan into a single tight screen — short bullet lines, no descriptions, no explanations. This becomes the version you screenshot or paste into your notes app.
💬 Example: *"Now compress the whole plan — both days plus the Sunday rain backup — into a one-screen version I can read on my phone. Each item is one short line. No descriptions, no flowery language. Order: Friday evening, Saturday morning/afternoon/evening, Sunday morning/afternoon, Sunday rain backup."*
You'll know it worked when the reply fits in roughly 12–18 short lines and reads like a checklist, not an essay.
If it looks different on your device: if the summary comes back too long, send a follow-up like "Cut that in half — keep only the place and the time."

## Step 6 — Move the plan out of the chat
A trip plan in a chat window is a plan you'll forget the moment you close the laptop. Send the one-screen summary out into a tool you actually open every day — your phone's notes app, a shared doc, or a calendar entry. This step takes 30 seconds and is the difference between a plan you read once and a plan you actually follow.
💬 Example: *"Now write me a copy-paste version of the one-screen summary that I can paste into Apple Notes or Google Keep. Use plain text, no markdown bold, one item per line, with a blank line between days."*
You'll know it worked when the reply is plain text you can select, copy, and paste into any notes app without reformatting.
If it looks different on your device: if Cohere still outputs markdown (bold headers, dashes), paste it into your notes app first, then strip the symbols manually — usually a 20-second job.

## Common mistakes
- **Asking for "the best" anything.** Cohere will confidently invent names. Always ask it to *describe* the cuisine and neighborhood instead — then look up real places yourself on a maps app or review site.
- **Regenerating when you meant to tweak.** The regenerate button (or any equivalent) throws away your working plan. Use it only when the whole direction is wrong, never to fix one line.
- **Trying to make one prompt do everything.** A single huge message gets a generic reply. Better: one structured ask, then a series of small follow-ups. Each follow-up is a small commitment you can keep or throw away.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** any time you face a vague-to-specific task — a birthday plan, a moving-day checklist, a guest's weekend visit — the same workflow works: short preamble, one structured ask, one tweak at a time, then a one-screen summary.
- **For your business or work:** the pattern translates directly to any project with a known shape and a few preferences — meeting agendas, conference prep, onboarding checklists. Set the preamble once for the project, then iterate.
- **If you want to go further:** next time, before sending your trip idea, paste in a small block of *your own* notes — a list of places a friend recommended, or three things you already booked — and ask Cohere to fit its suggestions around them. It gets dramatically more useful when you give it something real to anchor against.

## Try it now
Open Cohere and start a new chat. Type one sentence — your real, vague idea for a weekend, even if it's just "somewhere warm in February." Then paste the Step 1 preamble above it, followed by the Step 2 prompt structure with your destination filled in. Two minutes, and you'll have a draft you can react to.
